destination.name: Barrington Tops National Park
destination.tagline: A World Heritage rainforest plateau where snow gums and Antarctic beech grow above the Hunter and Manning valleys.
destination.description: Barrington Tops National Park covers about 765 square kilometres of subtropical rainforest, subalpine woodland and wilderness, and is the southernmost of the Gondwana Rainforests of Australia. Most of it is declared wilderness. Antarctic beech forest and mossy cascades grow at Gloucester Tops, and a 14 km track runs along the escarpment to Careys Peak, the highest point at 1,544 m. Snow usually falls on the peaks each year.
whyVisit: Walk the Antarctic Beech Forest loop

goodToKnow.title: Gravel roads, 4WD advised
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage says a 4WD is recommended on the gravel roads, and there are no shops inside the park, so bring food.

goodToKnow.title: Sections are not linked
goodToKnow.detail: The park's three sections are not connected by road; Central to Gloucester Tops can take three to four hours by car.

goodToKnow.title: Cold on the tops
goodToKnow.detail: Snow usually falls on the peaks each year and a record low of -17 C has been logged at 1,500 m.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Cooler, drier days in autumn and spring wildflowers make {months} good for walking; winter brings snow and frost on the tops.
